claims.claim: A carbon tax puts the cost of emissions where it belongs... Brindlewick cut household emissions by 14 percent...
Revenue returned as a flat dividend more than covers higher energy bills for the poorest households
Like cap-and-trade, a tax gives firms a price they can plan around
Economists across the spectrum prefer a tax to regulation because it lets each firm decide where abatement is cheapest
A carbon tax is regressive before any rebate arrives. Households reimbursed last, if at all.
Border adjustments require valuing carbon... no customs service has ever done at scale
The Brindlewick example proves that such a tax can slash household emissions by 14% in just two years
Revenue recycling as a flat dividend ensures the tax is progressive
The absence of functional border adjustments renders the tax a 'tax on competitiveness'
Rural communities face no behavioral incentive to change due to lack of substitutes
Tax is regressive before any rebate arrives... reimbursed last if at all
The Brindlewick gains are exceptional and not scalable
Absence of functional border adjustments makes the tax a flawed instrument
Every carbon tax passed so far has arrived with exemptions for the largest emitters... broad-based tax becomes a narrow one on households
